 BREAKING: Peoria Police retract person of interest being taken into custody in connection with explosive device found at BioUrja plant FBI takes lead in BioUrja bomb investigation 
 By Howard Packowitz Published : Nov. 13, 2026 at 6:47 PM CST | Updated : Nov. 14, 2026 at 8:37 PM CST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google PEORIA ( 25News Now ) - The FBI’s Springfield office is now in charge of the investigation of an explosive device found Friday at BioUrja’s ethanol plant in South Peoria. 
 The FBI made the announcement on its Facebook page Saturday night. 
 “ #FBISpringfield is now leading the investigation following the identification of an explosive device found at BioUrja Renewables on Friday, November 13. While the area has been cleared and no additional suspicious devices have been located, the FBI encourages the public to remain alert and share any relevant information they may have related to this ongoing situation by immediately calling 9-1-1, 1-800-CALL-FBI, or online at tips.fbi.gov. Tipsters may elect to remain anonymous. 
 The FBI continues to work closely with local, state, and federal law enforcement partners, to include ATF , Illinois Secretary of State , Illinois State Police Investigations , Peoria County Sheriff’s Office , Peoria IL Fire Department , and Peoria Police Department , to identify the individual(s) responsible and will hold them fully accountable under the law. 
 All releasable investigative updates will be shared via official FBI Springfield social channels." 
 Earlier on Saturday , Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixon announced the evacuation order had been lifted after bomb teams found no new explosives at the massive plant that is equivalent to 44 1/2 football fields. 
 Officials ordered the evacuation of a one-mile blast radius of the plant shortly after 7 p.m. Friday. 
 Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixon (Howard Packowitz | 25News Now) The police department released the following statement:
 “State, Federal, and Local Law Enforcement have done an extensive search of the BioUrja facility. They have found no other items of concern at this time. The evacuation order will no longer be in effect. The street barricades will be removed, and all roads will be opened. 
 Residents are now free to return to their homes in the area that was affected by this order. 
 Law Enforcement will continue their investigation into this incident and updates will be provided. 
 The Peoria Police Department thanks the community for their cooperation during this incident." 
 Dixon declined to reveal the type of device discovered Friday, only to say the package that was “rendered safe” was a “credible threat.”
 Peoria Mayor Rita Ali confirmed for reporters late Friday night that the device was a bomb. 
 Dixon also did not provide details of what he said was an extensive criminal investigation. Also participating the news conference were representatives of the FBI, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the U.S. Coast Guard, and the Peoria Fire Department. 
 Dixon said about 60 to 80 people were housed at the evacuation shelter at Manual High School. 
 No one sought shelter at EastSide Centre, East Peoria officials said. 
 East Peoria’s government released the following statement: 
 “As of 1:00 p.m., the 1-mile evacuation zone has been lifted and our residents can return to their homes and all businesses can resume normal operations. Once again, thank you to the East Peoria community for their continued patience and understanding during this situation. We are proud of our staff’s dedication to public safety and their actions to keep this community safe.”:
